title: Six days, one disc each
note: The page's ribbon of the six days of Hajj, the eighth to the thirteenth of Dhul Hijjah, each day a disc with its acts underneath.

lines.text: One ribbon, six days, the whole Hajj
Mina, from the eighth of Dhul Hijjah
lines.sub: staying at Mina is sunnah, nothing owed

lines.text: The ninth is Arafah: it cannot be missed
The tenth: stone, sacrifice, shave, tawaf
Tashriq: three days, all three pillars
After the twelfth, leave, or stay one more
lines.sub: leave Mina before sunset on the twelfth

lines.text: The farewell tawaf: three call it a duty
lines.sub: a sacrifice if left; sunnah for Maliki

lines.text: That slowness after the tenth is the point

lines.eyebrow: The six days, Mina and Arafah
lines.text: Each day is a disc with its acts below

research.retell: Hajj runs for six named days from the eighth to the thirteenth of Dhul Hijjah, each with its own acts, and the ninth at Arafah is the one day that cannot be missed.
proof: A ribbon of six days from the eighth to the thirteenth of Dhul Hijjah, each day a disc on the line with its acts listed underneath.
Makkah, then Mina; Yawm at-Tarwiyah, the day of watering
the one that cannot be missed; to Arafah until sunset; Muzdalifah, sleep there
Nahr; stone the large; the sacrifice; shave or shorten; tawaf al-ifadah; This is the second pillar of the Hajj and the one every school agrees on.
Tashriq; all three; stay at Mina; the takbir; Say the takbir aloud, in the camp and after every prayer
after the twelfth you may leave Mina, or stay for the thirteenth; the farewell
Hanafi, Shafi’i and Hanbali: the farewell tawaf is an obligation; whoever leaves without it owes a sacrifice. Maliki: it is a sunnah; nothing is owed by one who omits it.
After the tenth they feel slow, and that slowness is the point.
